entries.status_impact: document can never be uploaded; opaque error and no recovery path
entries.root_cause: LocalStorageService._validate_decodable projects the OCR render DPI (paddle_ocr_render_dpi=288 -> scale 4.0) and compares the DERIVED raster area against max_image_pixels (25,000,000). This document's page is 1117x1408 pt (1,572,736 sq pt); the budget allows <=1,562,500 sq pt, so it is rejected by 0.65%. The input-image pixel budget is conflated with the OCR render budget and the storage layer is made aware of OCR rendering.
entries.possible_improvement: Stop deriving the raster budget in the storage layer. Keep the per-page guard where the raster is produced (PaddleOCRProvider._check_pixels already does this) and let the separate cumulative max_pdf_render_pixels bound the document.

entries.status_impact: any metric computed on this file describes a fabricated specimen, not a real one
entries.root_cause: The file is named as a 4-day social-insurance payment certificate, but its content is a contribution-payment certificate issued by a Buddhist temple, carrying the canonical dummy business number and a literal sample-company name. It was evidently produced by the previous round's generator and placed beside the real files.
entries.possible_improvement: Label every realistic sample with a provenance class at ingest (REAL / RECREATED / SYNTHETIC) and report metrics per class.

entries.status_impact: blocks the student workflow's ONLY configured rule (issue_date <= 2026-12-31); 3 of 6 processable documents affected
entries.root_cause: BaseDocumentExtractor.issue_date_field guards its semantic fallback with a substring test over the WHOLE assembled document for any of its labels. The standard Certipia internet-issuance footer printed on every modern Korean university certificate contains the literal string for the issue-date label plus a suffix (meaning 'within N days of issue'), so the guard fires and returns the null labelled result; standalone_date_candidate, which correctly locates the date, is never consulted. Reproduced minimally: the same document yields the correct date with the footer removed and null with it present.
entries.possible_improvement: Make the guard row-scoped: treat a label as present only if it terminates a row that carries no value, and ignore footer/legal boilerplate rows. Do not substring-match the whole page.

entries.status_impact: a reliably readable field is guaranteed null on every SME certificate
entries.root_cause: SMEConfirmationExtractor passes its two representative labels in the wrong order. The matcher anchors the short label at the start of the longer label, leaves the label remainder as the value, and the PERSON_NAME shape validator rejects it; the matcher then breaks out of the label loop and never tries the compound label. Verified: short-first returns None, long-first returns the correct value. The business_registration extractor already fixed exactly this class with an explicit comment; the SME extractor did not.
entries.possible_improvement: Order compound labels first (longest-match-first) and make the matcher try every label of a field rather than breaking on the first shape-invalid one. Sweep all extractors for prefix-shadowed labels; 3 remain.

entries.actual_state: ALL SIX FIELDS UNRESOLVED (0 of 6 populated)
entries.status_impact: the highest-quality scan in the set produces the least output; a reviewer sees an effectively empty document
entries.root_cause: Two stages. (1) The detector cross-merged the adjacent table-column labels for student id and student name into one box, destroying both labels (OCR_SEGMENTATION). (2) build_rows then merged the entire header band - five logically separate fields - into ONE TextRow of 7 segments, because a table row's cells share a vertical extent and the row model has no concept of a table. Confirmed by dumping the grouped rows for this document.
entries.possible_improvement: This is the architecture gap, not a patchable bug: the row model cannot represent a table. Add a table-structure stage (PP-StructureV3 layout plus wired-table cell/structure recognition) and feed extractors a cell grid. As an interim guard, cap row merging by horizontal extent and require a plausible inter-segment gap.

entries.status_impact: the most important field of a business registration certificate is never populated; it is required and is a comparison source for the whole business workflow
entries.root_cause: The source is a 595x842 px (72 DPI) capture of a dense official form. The legal-entity-name label was recognised with two Hangul glyph substitutions and a moved parenthesis, so the extractor correctly refused to match. The dependency is upstream resolution, not extraction logic.
entries.possible_improvement: Add input-resolution guidance/validation (a 72 DPI A4 form cannot be read reliably by any recogniser) and/or route this document type to CLOVA OCR's purpose-built Korean business-registration specialised model. The current REVIEW_REQUIRED outcome is already the correct behaviour.

entries.status_impact: GPA is required for the configured transcript rule (>= 3.0) and can never be produced from a real transcript
entries.root_cause: The totals band and the header band are emitted as two separate horizontal rows, and the value order inside the band does not match the header order, so no label/value cell relation exists to exploit. On the low-resolution transcript the overall GPA cell sits three columns from its label. The candidate guard then saved the system: the top-ranked candidate was a per-semester average, several conflicting values existed, and the selector returned None instead of a confident wrong value. That guard is a genuine strength, not a defect.
entries.possible_improvement: Table-structure recognition so header and value cells can be associated by column. Keep the conflict-abstains guard exactly as it is.

entries.status_impact: two further documents lose their issue date for a reason unrelated to F-03
entries.root_cause: build_rows merged the bare issue date with adjacent boxes on the same visual band (REAL-002 with a seal/graphic artefact; REAL-003 with course-table text in a 9-segment row). standalone_date_candidate requires a date-ONLY row, so it declines. Row membership is decided purely by vertical overlap with no gap or height-ratio test, so a small stamp fragment and a full-width date count as one row.
entries.possible_improvement: Bound row merging by inter-segment horizontal gap and height ratio in addition to vertical overlap; then relax the date-only test for the issuance-block inference.

entries.status_impact: compounds F-08 on the transcript family
entries.root_cause: The issuance-anchor lookahead is a fixed 3 rows. On a dense transcript the issuer name sits further below the date because course-table rows interleave with the issuance block.
entries.possible_improvement: Make the anchor search independent of row count: scan the remaining rows on the page and require the first issuer-looking row to be within a bounded vertical distance rather than a fixed row count.

entries.evidence_problem: evidence is truthful (points at the mis-read row) but cannot reveal the substitution; nothing in the model detects it
entries.status_impact: company_name is REQUIRED for this type and is the target of a cross-document FIELD_COMPARISON. A reviewer who confirms the machine value produces a blocking INFORMATION_MISMATCH on a correct document.
entries.root_cause: The Korean PP-OCRv5 mobile recogniser substitutes two syllables on a 400x566 px capture of a letter-spaced legal-entity name. Published model accuracy on the Korean benchmark is 88.0 percent at LINE level (any wrong character fails the whole line), so per-character accuracy is materially lower. Nothing downstream can detect a fluent wrong string: the organisation validator only checks length, Hangul presence and digit count.
entries.possible_improvement: Keep the OCR-requires-confirmation gate, which is what stops this being dangerous. Add a per-field corroboration signal for identifiers (for example the business registration number appearing in the same table block as the company name) so the reviewer is told which fields corroborate each other. Do not attempt fuzzy repair.

entries.expected_state: PRESENT (adjudicated at 2.2x zoom: the bottom stroke of the first syllable is the horizontal vowel)
entries.evidence_problem: evidence truthful; recognition confidence 0.9955 is uninformative - the wrong value is the MOST confident value in the whole baseline
entries.status_impact: student_name is REQUIRED for this type and is compared with the project applicant name
entries.root_cause: A single Hangul vowel substitution on a clean, high-resolution scan. This is the clearest demonstration that OCR confidence is not a correctness probability: the single most confident machine value in the dataset is wrong.
entries.possible_improvement: No extraction change helps. This is the strongest argument for keeping OCR-sourced values permanently gated behind human confirmation and for surfacing an explicit per-field confidence caveat in the UI instead of a bare 0.99.

entries.evidence_problem: truthful but uninformative; FREE_TEXT validation accepts anything short enough, so a corrupted address passes every shape check
entries.status_impact: not consumed by any configured rule today; becomes dangerous the moment a rule references it
entries.root_cause: 72 DPI source. business_address is registered as FREE_TEXT with no structural validation (no administrative-unit pattern, no length band specific to addresses).
entries.possible_improvement: Give business_address a real validator (presence of the two-level Korean administrative suffix, plus a length band) so it is at least shape-checked and marked non-authoritative until reviewed.

entries.status_impact: two different documents submitted at the same time: the loser is permanently FAILED and must be manually re-processed. This is the ordinary failure mode for normal concurrent use.
entries.root_cause: The OCR worker is a single thread with a 1-permit semaphore. A second concurrent request raises OCR_BUSY, and DocumentProcessingService._fail converts a TRANSIENT capacity condition into a TERMINAL document state with no retry and no queue. Reproduced: two concurrent process calls yield one COMPLETED and one FAILED in 0.03 s; a manual retry then succeeds.
entries.possible_improvement: Treat OCR_BUSY as retryable: queue behind the worker, or return a retryable status that does not overwrite the document.

entries.status_impact: a realistic multi-page corporate submission pack cannot be processed at all
entries.root_cause: ocr_timeout_seconds=120 applies to the WHOLE document while a dense A4 page costs about 25.4 s on CPU at the configured 288 DPI render. Measured on this machine: 1 page 25.7 s OK, 3 pages 76.3 s OK, 6 pages FAILS at 120.0 s. The effective page limit is about 4, not the 30 that max_pdf_pages advertises. The timeout also keeps the single worker occupied, so the NEXT request also fails with OCR_BUSY - the cascade observed in the live log.
entries.possible_improvement: Decouple the budget from the worker: enqueue the job, keep the HTTP request short, and bound per-page cost instead of per-document. Raise the limit, lower the render DPI for multi-page documents, or scale the timeout with page count. Align max_pdf_pages with what the budget can actually serve.

entries.actual_state: only the started record, plus WARNINGs
entries.status_impact: no successful-processing audit trail exists in the deployed server; the per-page source-provenance record is never written
entries.root_cause: PaddleOCR model construction sets the ROOT logger level to WARNING. ADVS installs its structured JSON handler on the root logger, so after the first OCR call root.isEnabledFor(INFO) becomes False and every later record is dropped. Verified by snapshotting the root logger around one OCR call: level INFO -> WARNING, handler still attached, stderr still writable, no logging error emitted. Confirmed on the live server: a successful process emitted 1 record instead of 6.
entries.possible_improvement: Configure the application logger with its own handler and propagate=False, or re-assert the level after engine construction. One line; restores the entire per-stage audit trail.

entries.expected_state: a reviewer can resolve every machine-populated field
entries.status_impact: populated fields with no human exit; the document-level missing-field net can never close
entries.root_cause: FieldReviewService.target() rejects any field absent from EXPECTED_FIELDS for the document type. EXPECTED_FIELDS omits fields the extractors actually produce: business_address, business_type, business_item, issue_date, representative_name (business registration); certificate_number, issue_date, representative_name (SME); issue_date (both payment certificates). Because the evidence policy marks every OCR-sourced value REVIEW_REQUIRED and the default net then emits MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD for each nulled field, the document-level net cannot be satisfied for any OCR document.
entries.possible_improvement: Make EXPECTED_FIELDS the single vocabulary that extractors, reviewers and required-field defaults all derive from, so a field cannot be produced without being reviewable. Then scope MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD to the workflow's required fields instead of every field on the document.

entries.actual_state: two different semantics in one product
entries.status_impact: two correct documents can disagree by one space and produce a blocking INFORMATION_MISMATCH (severity ERROR -> NEEDS_CORRECTION)
entries.root_cause: ValidationEngine.validate_document compares names with a helper that strips all non-alphanumerics, while SubmissionVerificationEngine._field_comparison compares normalised values with exact string equality. normalize_text_field deliberately preserves internal whitespace, and OCR output legitimately contains internal spaces. Reproduced end-to-end through the engine: two equal company names differing by one space yield INFORMATION_MISMATCH.
entries.possible_improvement: Use one comparison helper for both scopes. Given the pre-check product position, the whitespace/punctuation-insensitive comparison is the right semantics; record the raw and compared forms in the issue so the reviewer sees what was ignored.

entries.status_impact: doubles OCR cost for legitimately sparse upright pages and contributes to the F-14 timeout cascade
entries.root_cause: _looks_orientation_broken returns True whenever a page yields fewer than 120 characters, regardless of mean confidence. A correct, upright but sparse page therefore always pays a second full inference pass plus construction of a second PaddleOCR pipeline inside the timed call.
entries.possible_improvement: Use confidence alone as the trigger, or require both low confidence and low character count, and warm the orientation engine outside the request budget.
